segments.narration: A carved wooden face survived 12,000 years in a bog. Workers hauled it out of Russian peat in 1890, in ten pieces.
Larch wood, nine feet tall, cut from a tree already 159 years old. Faces stare out of it at several heights, geometric lines running between them.
Nothing else from that era is like it. So who was carving portraits before anyone farmed, built a city, or fired a pot?
The answer is the bog. Peat sealed the larch from oxygen, so it never rotted. Hunter-gatherers made monumental art; we just never had the evidence.
In 2021, new radiocarbon dates put the carving at about 12,000 years old. Older than Stonehenge by seven thousand years.

verdicts.claim: The Shigir Idol was recovered from the Shigir peat bog on the eastern slope of the Middle Urals in 1890, in ten separate pieces.
verdicts.note: 75% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The idol is carved from larch wood, stands 2.8 m (about nine feet) as reconstructed, and carries multiple carved faces plus geometric ornament; the tree was at least 159 years old when felled.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia: larch, tree at least 159 years old when felled, 2.8 m (9.2 ft) as reconstructed, multiple faces with additional ones identified by Zhilin in 2014. Narration avoids a face count because sources differ.

verdicts.claim: The Shigir Idol is the oldest known wooden sculpture in the world.
verdicts.note: 100% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: The idol was made by hunter-gatherers, not by a farming or city-building society.
verdicts.note: 71% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: A 2021 study in Quaternary International by the University of Gottingen and the Russian Academy of Sciences dated the idol to roughly 12,000 years ago, far older than Stonehenge.
verdicts.note: 2021 Quaternary International study (Gottingen + Russian Academy of Sciences); reporting gives c. 12,100 years and notes it predates Stonehenge (c. 5,000 years old) by more than 7,000 years. Narration rounds to 'about 12,000'.
